Case report 1 is a 56-year-old woman with an endometrioid cancer who underwent a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy in 1998. She relapsed in the lung in 2014, 16 years from radical surgery.
Following multidisciplinary evaluation, the patient underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy with carboplatin area under the curve (AUC) 5 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m^(2) every 3 weeks.
Upon completion of 6 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy, in February 2015, the patient underwent right lung lobectomy.
Upon completion of 6 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy, in February 2015, the patient underwent right lung lobectomy.
Histopathology confirmed metastasis from endometrial carcinoma, which was ER positive, paired box 8 [PAX8] positive, thyroid transcription factor 1 [TTF-1] negative, and CDX2 negative (Fig. 2).
After surgery, the patient was prescribed endocrine therapy with tamoxifen 20 mg/day.
At the time of this writing, the patient is continuing hormonal treatment and oncological follow-up and remains disease free.

summary.text: A 56-year-old woman (age reference ambiguous) presented with abdominal swelling and pain, had a pelvic mass confirmed uterine, and underwent hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy without lymphadenectomy for a well-differentiated ER positive endometrioid cancer, FIGO stage IB, with negative margins; no adjuvant treatment was prescribed and follow-up was negative for 5 years.

In October 2014 she developed a chronic cough and chest CT showed a 90 mm right upper lobe mass; full staging showed no primary tumor or other metastases, and bronchoscopic biopsy showed ER positive endometrial carcinoma cells with Ki-67 positive in 30%. She received neoadjuvant carboplatin plus paclitaxel (partial response after three cycles, 6 cycles completed) and in February 2015 right lung lobectomy confirmed ER and PAX8 positive, TTF-1 and CDX2 negative metastasis from endometrial carcinoma with negative margins.
She was prescribed tamoxifen 20 mg/day after surgery and at the time of writing continues hormonal treatment and oncological follow-up and remains disease free.

Case report 2, a 75-year-old woman, with an endometrioid cancer, was treated by hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and adjuvant radiotherapy. The disease relapse in the lung was detected in 2019, 22 years from radical treatment.
In January 2019, the patient was admitted to the emergency department of our hospital because of worsening dyspnea.
Because of no other systemic metastases, in March 2019, the patient underwent surgical resection of the lesion.
After 4 months of follow-up, the patient developed a painful cutaneous node in the abdominal wall of the right hypochondrium.

A total-body CT scan showed a 45 mm in diameter lung mass near the site of metastasectomy, a 33 mm in diameter node of the abdominal wall, and other two smaller lesions in the muscles of the abdominal wall.
Because of systemic disease, our multidisciplinary team decided for first-line chemotherapy, which consisted of carboplatin AUC5 and paclitaxel 175 mg/m^(2) every 21 days.

summary.text: A 75-year-old woman (age reference ambiguous) had a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and lymphadenectomy in 1997 after accidental discovery of a pelvic mass; histology showed a grade 1 endometrioid carcinoma (ER and PAX8 positive, TTF-1 and CA125 negative), FIGO stage II with no distant metastasis on staging CT. She received adjuvant external beam radiotherapy (40 Gray) and 5 years of uneventful follow-up.

In January 2019 she was admitted to the emergency department with worsening dyspnea; chest computed angiography (while excluding pulmonary embolism) showed a 28 mm right upper lobe mass with PET SUV 12.2, and biopsy showed endometrial carcinoma cells. The lesion was surgically resected in March 2019 with clear margins and confirmed endometrial origin.

After 4 months of follow-up she developed a painful cutaneous node of the abdominal wall; CT showed a 45 mm lung mass near the metastasectomy site, a 33 mm abdominal wall node and two smaller abdominal wall muscle lesions. The node was removed and showed metastasis from endometrial carcinoma with vascular microemboli in adipose tissue. First-line carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy was decided for systemic disease and is ongoing at the time of writing.
